prompt: Let $R_i$ be the red graph at step $i$ of a valid contraction sequence $\sigma$ from a finite nonempty graph $G$ to one vertex. Which formula defines $\operatorname{tww}(G)$? Here $\Delta$ is maximum degree.

answers.explanation: Choose the best sequence, but control the worst red degree at every stage and every current vertex.
Twin-width optimises over the choice of sequence; it does not use the worst possible sequence.
The first and last red graphs are edgeless, so this would always be zero.
The definition bounds the peak, not the sum of red degrees over time.
Total red-edge count can be large while every red degree stays small.
The initial graph already has all input vertices; counting them measures input size rather than contraction errors.
Twin-width bounds red uncertainty. Black adjacency can be arbitrarily dense, as in a clique.
An average can hide a vertex with large red degree. The bound must hold at every vertex.
This bounds red component size, a stronger and different width measure.

answers.text: $\min_{\sigma}\max_i\Delta(R_i)$, with $\sigma$ restricted to merging adjacent vertices.
answers.explanation: Standard twin-width allows identification of nonadjacent vertices too; an edgeless graph must still admit a sequence.

sources.title: Bonnet et al. — Twin-width I, §§2–4 (2021 version)
